_about.what: Simulation parameters for the Froggy Turntable V12.5 (ROB 450 Team 03), generated from the CAD build of froggy-cad commit 357616d plus literature and vendor notes.
_about.frame: Same frame as model/exports/froggy_v12_5.glb, .step and .stl: millimetres, Z up, X/Y origin on the rotor spin axis, Z 0 = top face of the 2020 deck rails, +X = frog side, -Y = front panel. The GLB is NOT converted to glTF's Y-up metres: scale by 0.001 and rotate -90 deg about X if your loader assumes Y-up metres.
_about.units: Every number carries its unit in its key name (_mm, _deg, _kg, _g, _kg_m2, _rpm, _n_cm, _kpa, _ms, _s, _hz, _px) or in a sibling 'unit' field.
_about.sources: cad = value read from the V12.5 build (model/cad, sheet.json, assembly constants, lib/mass.py); camsim = model/exports/camsim/camsim.json; vendor = manufacturer page; literature = published papers, see frog.sources; decision = team decision not yet in CAD.

spin_axis.note: the rotor turns about the world Z axis through X = Y = 0

rotor.mass_note: volume x material density of every turning body (assembly rotor_mass_props, the same set as rotates_glb_nodes); lib/mass.py, which swaps some bought parts for catalogue masses, gives 1337.4 g for the 'rotor' module alone
rotor.izz_note: moment of inertia about the spin axis (Z) of the same set, from OCC volume properties at sheet densities

reflected_inertia_kg_m2.note: build's stop_profile: rotor Izz + motor rotor (82 g cm2 catalogue, assumed) + three PU rim wheels reflected at (89 / 12.05)^2; drive ratio 1:1

top_disc.exposed_note: the aluminium bezel ring lp_ring_top (ID 147, OD 186, 3.175 thick) sits on the disc from r 73.5 outward, so frogs stand on acrylic inside r 73.5

frog_on_disc.range_note: frog body anywhere from the axis out to 3 mm inside the bezel ID (the build's own placement limit); the camera sees the disc inside the tube bore r 72.5
frog_on_disc.load: shear (in the contact plane, radially outward)

frog_on_outside_wall.load: normal (pulls the frog radially off the outer tube wall); this is the normal-load test position
frog_on_outside_wall.cad_model_note: 45 mm snout-vent Agalychnis mesh stretched head to tail to 100 mm (the largest sponsor frog) as a clearance placeholder

rotor.fixed_note: everything not listed under rotates_* or belt is fixed to the frame
rotor.balance_note: rotor balance: rotor_cg_offset_mm=0.11 (CG x 0.01, y 0.11, z 93.1; turning mass 1.486 kg, Izz 0.00635 kg m2) by layout alone: the bank lies flat under the camera bridge, the Pi at +Y (the -Y LED driver is gone, I034), the switch at (-48, 40) and the port at (-52, -36) sit inside the tube, and the bank + bridge centre sits at (4, -3.1) so their moment squares what the Pi, port, switch, frogs and camera leave; no balance parts
rotor.frog_placeholders_note: mass_kg and izz_kg_m2 include the two placeholder frog meshes at their sheet density; subtract or replace them with your simulated frog

drum.material: clear cast acrylic tube, Rebower 145 ID x 150 OD x 14 in, cut to 140 mm
drum.surface: smooth acrylic (unscratched; scratches would turn the test into an interlocking test, requirement R6)
drum.refractive_index_note: typical PMMA value (literature), not measured; camsim ignores refraction

drum_posts.note: aluminium standoffs inside the tube, visible to the camera as the only rotor occluders

camera.model: Arducam UC-261 (OV5647 + LS-40180 fisheye, B0055 class)
camera.sensor: OmniVision OV5647, 1/4 in, 2592 x 1944, 1.4 um pixels (3.63 x 2.72 mm active)
camera.lens: LS-40180 M12 fisheye (Arducam UC-261 / B0055 class)
camera.fov_note: Arducam publishes only the horizontal FOV for the 1/4 in OV5647 board (194 deg). V is derived for an equidistant fisheye on the 4:3 sensor: 194 x 3/4 = 145.5 deg (EFL check: 2.72 mm / 1.05 mm = 148 deg). The sensor diagonal would map to 194 x 5/4 = 242.5 deg, but the LS-40180 image circle stops at 206 deg (Arducam's own D figure for this lens), so the corners beyond the 206 deg circle are dark; fov_diag_deg is that 206 deg circle. Measured on Sawyer's 2026-10-07 still at 1296 x 972: corner fall-off at radius 690 to 720 px, f = 648 px / 97 deg = 383 px/rad, so the circle is about 207 to 215 deg, consistent with 206.

fps.note: planned capture rate (FTIR contact-imaging plan: 30 to 60 fps needed); the OV5647 does 30 fps at 1920 x 1080 and up to 90 fps at 640 x 480 in Raspberry Pi camera modes (vendor). Not measured on the rotor yet.

camera.mount: co-rotating: rides on the carrier disc inside the drum on the printed fp9_camera_wedge_bridge, looking up and out through the acrylic top disc
camera.image_orientation: image width = sensor long axis (from the board), left -X / right +X

led_ring.type: WS2812B 16 x 5050 white LED ring (Adafruit NeoPixel Ring 16 footprint), 5 V
led_ring.position: coaxial with the lens on the camera bridge, LEDs along the optical axis, package tops 6.0 mm behind the lens front plane
led_ring.brightness_note: about 300 mA white with brightness capped near 30 percent

camsim_results.recommendation: As built (tilt 30 deg, lens 48 mm above the disc) the camera sees 99% of the top disc inside the tube and nothing on the rotor blocks either frog (100% / 100% of their camera-facing triangles unblocked; 65% / 63% are seen first, the rest hidden by the frogs' own legs), at 6.8 px/mm on the disc frog and 9.8 px/mm on the wall frog, so the placement works for both frogs. The best configuration of the sweep is tilt30_h66 (tilt 30 deg, h 66 mm: top disc 99%, disc frog 65% at 7.9 px/mm, wall frog 64% at 10.9 px/mm), scored on coverage of both frogs and the disc plus resolution. Resolution is not the limit: every configuration clear of its mount gives at least 6.8 px/mm on both frogs at the full 2592 x 1944 sensor (the brief's floor is 2); the lens heights below the bridge top (30 mm) put the lens inside fp9_camera_wedge_bridge and would need a new seat; steeper tilts push the -X edge of the top disc out of the frame (as_built 99%, tilt0_h48 99%, tilt15_h48 99%, tilt30_h48 99%, tilt45_h48 99%, tilt30_h66 99%). tilt30_h66 only buys about 15% more resolution, so the as-built 30 deg / 48 mm placement works and can stay.

motor.driver_note: the CAD still shows a CL42T-V41 body as the representative driver; the vendor torque curve was measured on a CL42T at 24 V

rotor_inertia_kg_m2.note: 82 g cm2 catalogue value for the 17HS19 family, assumed

torque_curve_24v.conditions: CL42T driver, 24 V, 2 A RMS, 2000 pulses/rev; typical values read from the factory chart

drive.type: GT2 timing belt, 2 mm pitch, 6 mm wide

decided_not_in_cad.status: decided, not yet implemented in the CAD or in these exports
decided_not_in_cad.motor_pulley: 30T GT2, 5 mm bore (Amazon, flange OD about 21.5, assumed until measured)
decided_not_in_cad.spindle_pulley: goBILDA 3422-4008-0030 30T GT2 REX 8 mm bore (flange OD 21, tooth OD 18.59, pitch dia 19.099, 18 long)
decided_not_in_cad.note: CAD check 2026-11-04: fits with no physical interference; belt to motor slab 4.0 mm; ratio stays 1:1 so rotor speed = motor speed

frog.species: grey tree frog, Hyla (Dryophytes) versicolor (the only species the sponsors named); the CAD placeholder mesh is Agalychnis callidryas
frog.working_case_mass_note: 35 g as used in the adhesion notes (the Litoria caerulea mass from Endlein et al. 2013); literature value
frog.earlier_small_case_note: 5 g grey tree frog used in the earlier sponsor back-calculations
frog.body_length_note: sponsor requirement R2: frogs 2 to 10 cm, optimised near 5 cm

total_pad_area_mm2.note: about 95 mm2 of toe pad on a 35 g L. caerulea (literature, Endlein et al. 2013 scale)

pad_shear_strength_kpa.note: 1.08 kPa single pads on glass (Federle 2006), 7.8 kPa on smooth resin (Crawford 2016), 30.1 kPa on 6 um roughness (Crawford 2016)

pad_normal_strength_kpa.note: 1.2 kPa whole animal on Perspex (Hanna & Barnes 1991), 1.7 kPa single pads on smooth resin (Crawford 2016)

sources: Hanna G, Barnes WJP (1991) J Exp Biol 155:103-125
Federle W et al. (2006) J R Soc Interface 3:689-697
Endlein T et al. (2013) J R Soc Interface 10:20120838
Crawford N et al. (2016) Beilstein J Nanotechnol 7:2006-2016
frog.estimate_note: orchestrator arithmetic (not a measurement): on smooth acrylic a 35 g frog slips at roughly 0.3 to 2 g (about 75 to 190 rpm at 50 mm); the wall frog detaches at roughly 0.4 to 1 g (about 65 to 105 rpm at 75 mm)

targets.speed_note: team requirement; the literature numbers above suggest a smooth-acrylic frog detaches well below this
targets.latency_note: target from detection of slip to the start of controlled deceleration; past it, lower rotor speed and enlarge the catch

centripetal_acceleration.formula: a = omega^2 * r, omega = 2 * pi * rpm / 60 (rad/s), r in m; in g: a / 9.80665

ramp_profiles_used.name: Oct 21 bench UI ramps (bare 17HS08)
ramp_profiles_used.note: four logged ramps stopped during acceleration at about 93 rpm commanded, stop phase about 0.45 s

ramp_profiles_used.name: CAD motor-only stop estimate from 400 rpm
ramp_profiles_used.note: UNQUALIFIED analytical estimate: vendor 31.5 N cm at 400 rpm / 1.2 margin over the total spindle inertia; not belt qualified
